For a **pellet smoker**, I’d choose a station with at least **1,000Wh of capacity** and enough inverter output for the smoker’s startup surge. Pellet grills usually draw modest power once running, but the igniter can briefly demand much more. One guide estimates a 12-hour cook at roughly **450–750Wh**, with cold or windy conditions pushing consumption up. ([Dealectric](https://dealectric.com/power-station-to-run-a-pellet-smoker-overnight); [Volt & Valley](https://voltandvalley.com/tailgate-travel/best-power-station-for-a-pellet-grill))

- **Best bet for overnight plus campsite extras: BLUETTI Elite 200 V2.** Its **2,073.6Wh capacity and 2,600W inverter** give you a useful cushion for a long cook, and leave capacity for lights or charging devices. [Buy the Elite 200 V2](https://dealectric.com/go/bluetti-elite-200-v2)
- **Smaller option for one overnight cook: BLUETTI AC180.** At **1,152Wh**, it’s a reasonable pick if you mainly need to run the smoker and your grill’s actual draw is in the expected range. [Buy the AC180](https://dealectric.com/go/bluetti-ac180)

Before buying, check your smoker’s label or manual for its **startup/igniter wattage**—a small station with a 300W inverter may be marginal even if the grill’s running draw is low. Runtime also drops if you power other gear or encounter cold, windy weather.
